metadata.title: Secure‑Resilience Platform SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan establishing Secure‑Resilience as the authoritative framework for determining safe recovery, continuity, halt, isolation, and resumption across all enterprise domains.

import-profile.remarks: This SSPP inherits the Operational Resilience composite pattern, which assembles Secure‑Resilience foundational semantics and governed solution patterns.

system-characteristics.system-description: The Secure‑Resilience Platform defines when recovery, restoration, continuity, degradation, halt, isolation, or decommissioning actions are permitted. It applies uniformly across IT systems, integrations, and cyber‑physical devices, ensuring recovery actions never introduce new harm or violate safety or regulatory authority.

props.name: platform-role
props.remarks: Authoritative plane governing resilience eligibility and permitted outcomes.

props.name: resilience-model
props.remarks: Safe outcomes always supersede availability, speed of recovery, or service continuity.

props.name: implicit-recovery
props.remarks: Backup availability, DR capability, or continuity plans must not imply permission to restore, fail over, or resume.

props.name: default-on-uncertainty
props.remarks: When eligibility cannot be conclusively established, halt or isolation is the default outcome.

props.name: resume-requirement
props.remarks: Resumption of operation requires explicit resume eligibility and authorization.

props.name: recall-precedence
props.remarks: Recall or authority-driven withdrawal from service suppresses restore and resume unconditionally.

props.name: coordination-guidance
props.remarks: Cyber incident coordination guidance informs communication and escalation but does not authorize recovery or resumption.

system-implementation.remarks: The Secure‑Resilience Platform is implemented through decision gating and signal interpretation. It does not perform recovery operations or define tooling. Enforcement occurs through downstream solution patterns and relying systems.

roles.title: Resilience Architecture
roles.remarks: Defines resilience semantics, non‑equivalence rules, and permitted outcomes.

roles.title: Resilience Governance
roles.remarks: Approves resume eligibility criteria, recall handling, and safety precedence across domains.

roles.title: Resilience Operations
roles.remarks: Executes recovery and continuity actions strictly as permitted by Secure‑Resilience eligibility decisions.

roles.title: Resilience Monitoring
roles.remarks: Monitors eligibility signals, unsafe recovery attempts, and violations of resilience constraints.

control-implementation.remarks: Controls are satisfied through constrained interpretation of NIST SP 800‑53 CP family controls. This SSPP introduces no new control requirements and performs no direct enforcement.
